mode: recorded inference; no model executes in this interface

provenance.task: Describe visible geometry and locate morphology, inscription, damage and possible motifs. Separate observation from conventional label; abstain where uncertain. No OCR, translation, restoration or historical attribution.
provenance.review_status: Human scholarly adjudication pending; no corrections or approvals recorded.

model_limitations: Bounding boxes are approximate and normalized to the full attached photographs, with the origin at the upper left.
A single view of each face limits separation of shallow carving from shadows, pitting, and abrasion.
Proposed labels are visual comparisons only. No inscription is transcribed or translated, and no missing forms, material composition, or historical attribution are inferred.

objects.date_basis: Museum catalogue range; not an inscription-internal date
objects.catalogue_description_paraphrase: Fragment with triangular pediment and lateral acroteria. Raised hand/forearm above inscription; Tanit sign between two caducei below it. Light limestone. Carthage; Tophet attribution uncertain.
objects.original_script_status: No independently verified original-script transcription; photograph is the material witness, not a transcription.

text_annotation.method: assistant-authored source annotation, not model OCR
text_annotation.observation: Divine recipients, ll. 1–2; vow, donor and genealogy, ll. 2–4. The text and lower motif belong to the same monument, but their association does not prove the sign depicts the named deity.

objects.uncertainty: DBDMLK is printed in l. 3 and interpreted as ʿBDMLK by the catalogue. Final BN ṢR: catalogue renders “son of Tyre”; museum record interprets family origin as Tyre. Do not silently turn this into a verified migration history.
abstentions: No conventional label assigned to the upper curve or the carvings flanking the central form.
Small angular marks near the base are too ambiguous to classify as separate motifs.
No damaged contours or inscription signs reconstructed.

regions.observation: Broad slab with a central tapered projection and a blunt, uneven crest. Lower rounded projections flank it on both shoulders. The lower sides are nearly upright, and the base has a pronounced central notch.
regions.uncertainty: The clips cover parts of both edges. Chipping obscures the original profiles of the crest, shoulders, and base.

regions.legibility: Four sloping rows are distinguishable across the middle of the face. Many individual grooves are clear, but several signs are incomplete or difficult to separate from nearby marks.
regions.uncertainty: Surface losses interrupt parts of the rows. Long oblique strokes extend into the spaces between them.

regions.observation: Rough, pitted areas across the crest and shoulders, with patches of apparent surface loss above the inscription.
regions.uncertainty: The region includes both rough and smoother patches; the photograph does not distinguish all losses from original surface texture.

regions.observation: Irregular surface losses intersect the carved loops and curves below the inscription on the right.
regions.uncertainty: The boundary between abrasion and shallow carving is unclear in places.

regions.observation: Chipping along the lower left edge and an uneven, notched base.
regions.uncertainty: The original base profile is indeterminate.

regions.observation: A short, upward-opening curved groove lies on the centerline immediately above the first inscription row.
regions.uncertainty: The lower curve is clearer than its tips. The rough surface above it prevents identification of a complete shape.
regions.comparison: partial curve only; catalogue hand/forearm not recovered

regions.observation: A large outlined form widens toward a slightly bowed base. A horizontal bar crosses its narrow upper end, and a small rounded arc rises above the center of the bar.
regions.uncertainty: The arrangement of the main elements is clear, but the label is a conventional comparison of shapes. The ends of the horizontal bar are less clear.
regions.comparison: conventional label broadly concordant with catalogue; not independent validation

regions.observation: Two vertically stacked loop-like outlines stand above a broad curve with outward-turning ends, to the left of the large central form.
regions.uncertainty: The loops are distinct, but short interruptions make their closure and connection to the lower curve uncertain.
regions.comparison: geometric correspondence only; conventional label abstained

regions.observation: Fragments of stacked rounded outlines and outward-curving strokes appear to the right of the large central form.
regions.uncertainty: Losses interrupt several contours. The better-preserved left carving does not establish the missing portions on the right.
regions.comparison: geometric correspondence only; conventional label abstained

objects.date_basis: Museum catalogue range; not an inscription-internal date
objects.catalogue_description_paraphrase: Fragment; fluted column shafts border the inscription. Lower horizontal agricultural implement, possibly a cart, according to the catalogue. Ochre limestone. Carthage; Tophet attribution uncertain.
objects.original_script_status: No independently verified original-script transcription; photograph is the material witness, not a transcription.

text_annotation.method: assistant-authored source annotation, not model OCR
text_annotation.observation: Restored divine recipient, ll. 1′–2′; vow and donor name split across ll. 2′–3′; genealogy, ll. 3′–4′. An agricultural-looking motif does not establish the donor’s occupation.

objects.uncertainty: CIS 969 in catalogue heading and museum identifiers; CIS 963 in museum bibliography. Catalogue uncertain strokes in ll. 1′–2′ differ from simplified museum transcription. Photograph title says plough; catalogue suggests cart; vision model suggests vessel. None is independent ground truth.
abstentions: No motif identified on the damaged upper face.
No firm inscription line count assigned.
No specific vessel type or function assigned to the lower carving.

regions.observation: Broad upright slab with inward-sloping upper sides, an uneven flattened crest, and an irregular base. A broad area of apparent surface loss occupies the upper face and meets the inscription along a jagged diagonal boundary.
regions.uncertainty: The clips obscure parts of the lateral edges. The surviving crest does not establish the original top profile.

regions.legibility: Three row bands can be distinguished below the damaged upper surface: a fragmentary upper band, a clearer middle band, and a short lower band visible on the right. Isolated cuts above them at upper right may belong to another row.
regions.uncertainty: The upper break truncates the layout. The isolated upper cuts do not support a firm total, and some strokes in the surviving bands are incomplete.

regions.observation: Broad, uneven upper surface with a jagged lower boundary that crosses the upper inscription area.
regions.uncertainty: The photograph does not show how much of the original face was removed or whether any carving preceded the loss.

regions.observation: Irregular rough patch in the lower middle of the inscription panel, near the short bottom row.
regions.uncertainty: Shallow grooves and the margins of the rough patch are difficult to distinguish.

regions.observation: Uneven, chipped lower edge beneath the large carved design.
regions.uncertainty: The original base profile is indeterminate.

regions.observation: A narrow, nearly vertical strip with parallel grooves and a widened, stepped foot borders the inscription on the left.
regions.uncertainty: The foot and shaft are clearer than the damaged upper end.
regions.comparison: conventional label broadly concordant with catalogue; not independent validation

regions.observation: Several long parallel vertical grooves form a band on the right of the inscription, with a widened foot above a horizontal division.
regions.uncertainty: Some outer grooves merge with the damaged margin, and the upper termination is incomplete.
regions.comparison: conventional label broadly concordant with catalogue; not independent validation

regions.observation: Below the panel is a long shallow curved band that rises to a pointed left end. Toward the center and right, a straighter upper band and repeated short near-vertical strokes sit above the curved baseline.
regions.uncertainty: The long curved profile supports the comparison, but wear interrupts the upper details. The roles of the short strokes and the form of the right end are unclear.
regions.comparison: interpretive disagreement: vessel-like vs catalogue possible cart; unresolved, not certified model error

objects.date_basis: Museum catalogue range; not an inscription-internal date
objects.catalogue_description_paraphrase: Fragment with triangular pediment; an anthropomorphized motif at the top, probably derived from the bottle-idol sign. Pale grey limestone. Carthage; Tophet attribution uncertain.
objects.original_script_status: No independently verified original-script transcription; photograph is the material witness, not a transcription.

text_annotation.method: assistant-authored source annotation, not model OCR
text_annotation.observation: Divine recipients, ll. 1–3; vow and donor name, ll. 3–4; BT, “daughter of”, l. 4. The catalogue describes a female dedication. This does not identify the carved figure as the donor.

objects.uncertainty: The two catalogues vocalize the donor’s name differently (Bitinaʿmat / Batnaʿmat). Retain consonants; no original-script transcription independently verified.
abstentions: No conventional label assigned to the upper carving or the broad arc.
No missing contour or damaged inscription signs reconstructed.

regions.observation: Tall slab with a tapered, slightly rounded apex, sloping shoulders, roughly upright lower sides, and an irregular base. The face is pitted, with larger losses along the left side and both lower corners.
regions.uncertainty: The bounding box excludes the mount. The clips hide short stretches of the side edges, and the photograph does not establish the original outline at chipped edges.

regions.legibility: Partly legible at the stroke level. Four rows are readily distinguishable, and a fifth survives in part along the broken base.
regions.uncertainty: Long strokes project between rows, and losses at the sides and base interrupt several signs. Five is a count of visible rows only.

regions.observation: Cluster of irregular depressions and edge losses on the left side above the inscription.
regions.uncertainty: Individual losses have diffuse boundaries.

regions.observation: Deep irregular losses along the lower left edge, beside and across the ends of inscription rows.
regions.uncertainty: The amount of inscription lost cannot be determined.

regions.observation: Broad stepped loss at the lower right corner extending into the bottom row.
regions.uncertainty: The original corner shape is indeterminate.

regions.observation: A short horizontal bar with downturned ends sits above a compact set of curved and angular grooves. The lower outline narrows to a point where it meets the broad arc below.
regions.uncertainty: The grooves are visible, but their exact joins and whether they form a single motif are uncertain.
regions.comparison: geometric correspondence only; conventional label abstained

regions.observation: A wide arch-shaped groove curves downward from the center toward both sides. Fainter, near-vertical traces lie below its ends.
regions.uncertainty: The curved groove is clear. The faint side traces are intermittent, so their connection to the arc cannot be established.
regions.comparison: geometric correspondence only; conventional label abstained
